items_missed: No agenda statement at all - never told Adam what the call would cover or roughly how long it would take, and never asked 'sound good?' Went straight from hello into the walkthrough policy.
Never confirmed date availability. Adam raised the 22nd vs the 23rd and asked about a Monday, and Daniel answered with rate differences but never said whether any of those dates were actually open.
Never asked about packing services. Adam volunteered that everything would be boxed on arrival, so the rep never had to ask - a real packing sale could have been missed here.
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops.
No moving-stressor question - never asked what Adam was worried about, on a call where Adam opened by saying he was shopping four quotes and needed to lock something in immediately.
No 'pricing is super simple' framing before the rate.
On-Time Guarantee stated as 'we won't be hours and hours late or flat out cancel' - never said Einstein starts discounting if it misses the arrival window, which is the actual differentiator.

No direct booking ask. Said 'if you do decide, we don't do deposits to go on the schedule' instead of 'we have the 23rd open, want me to lock it in?' - on a live comparison-shopping call where Adam said he needed to decide now.
Never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or asked Adam to reply with corrections to verify the info.
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Never gave office hours or how to reach the branch.
Used Adam's name only once, in the opening line.
Insurance explained as $2,000 No Worries coverage only - no 60 cents per pound baseline for contrast.
top_strength: Elite discovery and estimate reasoning. Adam refused the virtual walkthrough on a ~1,900 sqft home, and Daniel recovered by walking him room by room, catching the leaf in the dining table, the garage inventory, and what was going upstairs at BOTH locations - then showed his work on the estimate, explaining that square footage alone would normally push this to two trucks and four movers but the real inventory and access supported two movers and one truck at seven to eight hours ($1,470-$1,680), with the interior stairwells named as the driver.
coaching_note: Daniel earns the sale in discovery and then lets it walk out the door at the close. Adam said on the call he was on his fourth quote that day and needed to land something now, and Daniel still ended with 'sounds like a plan, I'll send the email' instead of asking for the booking. Next call: once the estimate is out, ask directly for the date - 'I've got the 23rd open, no deposit, want me to hold it for you?' - then close with the email recap, a reply-with-corrections ask, and 'any other questions before I let you go?'
phone_presence_notes: Genuinely patient and low-pressure - opened the call conceding the competitor race with 'it's part of the game,' told Adam 'take your time, I'd rather have the accurate estimate,' and complimented his dimensions, though he used Adam's name only once and never matched the customer's stated urgency.
